result.summary: This Development Agreement outlines terms for bio-catalyst development services between Cargill and Bioamber over a four-year term. The agreement includes milestone payments, confidentiality provisions, intellectual property guidelines, and non-compete commitments. Certain playbook requirements such as liability caps and specific indemnity terms are not addressed in the provided excerpts, posing potential risk exposures.

parties.name: Cargill, Incorporated, Bio Technology Development Center

categoryScores.comment: R-V-LIAB-01 Not Addressed: The provided contract excerpts do not contain a limitation of liability clause.
R-V-INDEM-01 Not Addressed: The provided contract excerpts do not contain an intellectual property indemnification clause.
R-V-TERM-01 Pass: The contract establishes a firm four-year term with termination restricted to specific defaults and bankruptcy events.
R-V-IP-01 Pass: The provisions properly protect proprietary rights and background technology.
R-V-PAY-01 Pass: Payment terms adhere to the Net 30 standard set out in the playbook.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Represents Bioamber's interests in securing robust development rights and remedies.
agentPerspectives.stance: Aggressive on milestone oversight and research license options.
keyPoints: Leverages option to research license if milestones are missed.
Ensures strict non-compete limits on Cargill's development of conflicting microorganisms.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Maintain strict oversight on milestone achievements and enforce penalty limitations.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Focuses on closing the alliance and ensuring smooth operational execution.
agentPerspectives.stance: Supportive of the collaborative structure and milestone-based compensation.
keyPoints: Secures steady FTE funding streams over the four-year term.
Establishes clear pathways for commercial licensing via Exhibit D.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Keep payment schedules tied strictly to verified milestones and invoiced expenses.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Evaluates contract against standard vendor protection guardrails.
agentPerspectives.stance: Cautious due to missing liability caps and indemnity clauses.
keyPoints: Rule R-V-LIAB-01 is not addressed in the provided excerpts.
Rule R-V-INDEM-01 lacks an explicit IP indemnity framework.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Introduce standard vendor liability caps and limited IP indemnification before final execution.

redlines.originalText: Bioamber and Cargill agree to waive any and all claims against each other for consequential, punitive, incidental, special, or other forms of "exemplary" losses
redlines.proposedText: Bioamber and Cargill agree to waive any and all claims against each other for consequential, punitive, incidental, special, or other forms of exemplary losses without carve-outs.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: The carve-out for gross negligence and willful misconduct is standard under applicable law and necessary to prevent moral hazard.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Broad carve-outs undermine the predictability of the limitation of liability cap.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Aligns the limitation of liability with our strict vendor protection playbook.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We require a mutual clean waiver of consequential damages to maintain predictable risk profiles.

redlines.originalText: a work assignment from any third party shall not be accepted, or work by Cargill aloneshall not be conducted, to develop CB1 or other microorganisms
redlines.proposedText: Cargill may accept third-party work subject to standard confidentiality protections.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: This exclusivity provision is the core commercial protection for Bioamber's proprietary technology and is essential to the transaction.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Overly restrictive exclusivity hinders our operational freedom and creates third-party breach risks.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Narrows the restriction to protect core IP without totally barring third-party engagements.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can agree to protect your specific IP while maintaining standard operational freedom.

redlines.originalText: Upon the request of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party will destroy all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party and any documents prepared by the Receiving Party
redlines.proposedText: Upon request, the Receiving Party will return or destroy Confidential Information, excluding archival legal copies.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: This is standard protection for sensitive proprietary information and R&D data.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Destroying all derivative work documents burdens our compliance and internal record-keeping.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Permits standard legal archival exceptions while satisfying return obligations.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: Allowing standard legal archival copies is market practice for compliance.

redlines.originalText: If Cargill waives its option to prepare and prosecute a patent application in accordance with Section 5.2.3 and elects not to file such a patent application
redlines.proposedText: If Cargill elects not to file a patent application, Cargill shall give Bioamber notice within a reasonable timeframe.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: Bioamber must have the right to protect its intellectual property if Cargill elects not to maintain patent filings.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Lengthy advance notice periods create operational burdens and rigid timelines.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Streamlines notice requirements while preserving Bioamber's right to take over filings.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can provide timely notice without being locked into rigid advance windows.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: The Receiving Party agrees to take and maintain proper and appropriate steps to protect Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Confidentiality — Mutual Confidentiality with Standard Exclusions
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Each party shall hold the other party's Confidential Information in confidence, use it only to perform this Agreement, and disclose it only to employees and advisers who need to know it and are bound by equivalent duties.
deviations: Lacks explicit survival duration details in the immediate text excerpt.
missingProtections: Standard exclusions are partially covered but standard duration is not explicitly five years in the main excerpt.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Ensure standard carve-outs and explicit survival terms are clearly aligned with mutual standards.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: Bioamber will pay Cargill's costs within thirty (30) days of receipt of invoice and supporting documentation.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Payment & Milestones — Net 30 Invoicing with Milestone Acceptance Signoff
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Invoicing and Payment. Provider shall invoice Customer in accordance with the Payment Schedule set forth in Exhibit A. All undisputed amounts shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days from the date of receipt of a valid itemized invoice ('Net 30').
deviations: Uses FTE and milestone structures specific to a development agreement rather than standard SaaS net 30 invoicing.
missingProtections: Explicit milestone acceptance signoff periods are tied to specific development deliverables rather than general acceptance terms.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Retain custom development payment and milestone terms as tailored for this R&D agreement.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: Upon the request of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party will destroy all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: IP Rights — Customer Work Product Ownership & Non-Use of Customer Data for AI Training
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (b) Customer Data & AI Model Boundaries. Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data. Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, improve, or benchmark any generalized artificial intelligence.
deviations: Focuses on confidentiality and destruction of information rather than modern AI training restrictions.
missingProtections: No explicit restriction on using customer data for training artificial intelligence models.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Add a specific restriction against using customer data for AI model training if applicable to the services.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: Sections 4 (Confidentiality), 5 (Intellectual Property), 6 (WRF Patents), 7 (Warranties), 8 (Indemnification), 13.2 (Governing Law), and 13.7 (Survivability) will survive the expiration or earlier termination.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Provisions which by their nature should survive termination, including confidentiality, indemnification, limitation of liability, payment of accrued fees, data return and deletion, and governing law, survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement.
deviations: Lists specific section numbers instead of general categories of clauses.
missingProtections: Explicit mention of limitation of liability and payment of accrued fees in the survival clause.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Ensure all standard post-termination obligations are explicitly covered in the survival clause.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: Bioamber and Cargill agree to waive any and all claims against each other for consequential, punitive, incidental, special, or other forms of exemplary losses.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Indemnification — Market Mutual IP & Third-Party Indemnification
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Provider Indemnification. Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer... from and against any third-party claims, suits, or proceedings...
deviations: Section 8 frames the provision as a waiver of consequential damages rather than a standard third-party IP defense indemnification.
missingProtections: Mutual third-party intellectual property infringement indemnification is missing from the excerpt.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Incorporate standard mutual third-party IP indemnification obligations.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: Cargill shall have no liability to Bioamber for Bioamber's acts or failure to act with respect to such Third Party Patents.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Non-Compete — No Non-Compete; Narrow Non-Solicitation Only
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Nothing in this Agreement restricts either party from developing, acquiring or marketing products or services that compete with the other party's...
deviations: The agreement actually contains strict non-compete commitments for Bioamber in section 13.9 rather than omitting them.
missingProtections: Freedom to compete is restricted by specific project-based non-compete clauses.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Review the specific non-compete scope in Section 13.9 to ensure it aligns with business goals.

rules.explanation: The provided contract excerpts do not contain a limitation of liability clause.
rules.recommendation: Add a limitation of liability clause capping total liability at the amounts received in the preceding 12 months and disclaiming consequential damages.

rules.explanation: The provided contract excerpts do not contain an intellectual property indemnification clause.
rules.recommendation: Insert a limited scope IP indemnity clause protecting the vendor against infringement claims conditioned on prompt notice and sole defense control.

rules.evidence: This Development Agreement will begin on the Effective Date and continue for four (4) years unless earlier terminated pursuant to Section 10.2
rules.explanation: The contract establishes a firm four-year term with termination restricted to specific defaults and bankruptcy events.

rules.evidence: All documents and/or tangible materials containing or comprising Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party will remain the property of the Disclosing Party.
rules.explanation: The provisions properly protect proprietary rights and background technology.

rules.evidence: Bioamber will pay Cargill's costs within thirty (30) days of receipt of invoice and supporting documentation.
rules.explanation: Payment terms adhere to the Net 30 standard set out in the playbook.

missingProtections.title: Renewal with Reminder and Short Opt-Out Notice
missingProtections.standardText: This Agreement renews for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the current term. The Provider shall send a written renewal reminder, including any price change, at least sixty (60) days before each renewal date. Renewal fees may not increase by more than the lower of five percent (5%) or the applicable consumer price index.
missingProtections.evidence: The contract sets a fixed term of four years without automatic renewal or renewal reminder mechanisms.

missingProtections.title: Data Return and Transition Assistance on Exit
missingProtections.standardText: On expiry or termination for any reason, the Provider shall, for up to ninety (90) days: make all Customer Data available for export in a commonly used, machine-readable format at no extra charge; provide reasonable transition assistance at its then-current rates; and afterwards delete Customer Data from its systems and certify deletion in writing, except where retention is required by law.
missingProtections.evidence: The contract contains standard confidentiality return provisions but lacks comprehensive transition assistance and data export obligations on exit.

opposingFindings.quote: Bioamber and Cargill agree to waive any and all claims against each other for consequential, punitive, incidental, special, or other forms of "exemplary" losses whether arising in contract, warranty, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, including any losses relating to lost use, lost profits, lost business, damage to reputation, or lost or diminished financing unless such claims are based on a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
opposingFindings.issue: The mutual waiver of consequential damages contains a broad carve-out for gross negligence or willful misconduct that weakens the liability protection for our client.
opposingFindings.leverage: The carve-out for gross negligence and willful misconduct is standard under applicable law and necessary to prevent moral hazard.

opposingFindings.quote: a work assignment from any third party shall not be accepted, or work by Cargill aloneshall not be conducted, to develop CB1 or other microorganisms that will be used to (a) directly produce succinic acid and salts thereof, or (b) indirectly produce succinic acid and salts thereof
opposingFindings.issue: This restriction severely limits Cargill's freedom to accept third-party work related to microorganisms for succinic acid production.
opposingFindings.leverage: This exclusivity provision is the core commercial protection for Bioamber's proprietary technology and is essential to the transaction.

opposingFindings.quote: Upon the request of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party will destroy all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party and any documents prepared by the Receiving Party using Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party and the Receiving Party agrees to provide confirmation of such destruction in writing.
opposingFindings.issue: The obligation to destroy all documents prepared using Confidential Information upon request is overly broad and burdensome.
opposingFindings.leverage: This is standard protection for sensitive proprietary information and R&D data.

opposingFindings.quote: If Cargill waives its option to prepare and prosecute a patent application in accordance with Section 5.2.3 and elects not to file such a patent application or elects to allow any such patent application or issued/granted patent to become abandoned or lapse, Cargill shall give Bioamber notice of such election promptly and at least two (2) months prior
opposingFindings.issue: Cargill is forced to give lengthy advance notice and surrender control of patent prosecution to Bioamber if it decides not to proceed.
opposingFindings.leverage: Bioamber must have the right to protect its intellectual property if Cargill elects not to maintain patent filings.
